summary_html: Federal **Child and Family Services Reviews (CFSR)** monitor state performance on safety, permanency, and well-being. Project Milk Carton flags states that repeatedly fail or never publish CFSR improvement plans.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court held that the Adoption Assistance and Child Welfare Act's requirement that states make reasonable efforts to prevent removal and reunify families creates no right enforceable by private individuals under section 1983 or directly under the Act.
key_cases.relevance: It explains why CFSR performance failures are addressed administratively rather than in private litigation.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the Act does not create an enforceable right on behalf of respondents.

key_cases.case_name: Georgia Department of Human Services v. Spruill
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court of Georgia reversed the Court of Appeals and held that the Georgia Tort Claims Act's discretionary function exception preserved sovereign immunity for a DFCS caseworker's choices in investigating a report of child neglect, barring the tort suit brought after the children were severely injured.
key_cases.relevance: It shows that Georgia's performance failures in investigation are not remediable through state tort litigation.
key_cases.quote: But when such agents act as representatives of the sovereign, they exercise a different sort of discretion, one that may be informed in significant part by considerations of public policy.

key_cases.case_name: Perdue v. Kenny A. ex rel. Winn
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court reversed the Eleventh Circuit in the Georgia foster-care class action, holding that a lodestar fee under 42 U.S.C. 1988 may be enhanced for superior attorney performance only in rare and exceptional circumstances supported by specific evidence, and that the district court's 75 percent enhancement was not properly justified.
key_cases.relevance: It is the United States Supreme Court's decision in the very litigation that produced Georgia's foster-care consent decree and its independent accountability agents, and it governs what plaintiffs' counsel can recover for driving that kind of systemic reform.
key_cases.quote: In the present case, the District Court did not provide proper justification for the large enhancement that it awarded.
